strengths: Novel problem formulation handling parameter-dependent PDE constraints without paired training data - a genuine advance over prior work limited to global constraints
Strong theoretical foundation with principled application of Adjoint Matching framework to physics-constrained generative modeling via stochastic optimal control

Comprehensive experimental evaluation within scope including diverse tasks (denoising, guidance, super-resolution, misspecification) with ablations and quantitative metrics showing substantial residual reduction

Thoughtful technical design with elegant surrogate base flow construction for joint parameter evolution, computationally efficient weak-form residuals via Wendland wavelets, and detailed implementation documentation
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and promise of code release supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Severely limited experimental scope with only 2 canonical benchmark PDEs (Darcy, Acoustics) on modest grids; no demonstration on complex multi-physics, coupled systems, or real observational data

Critical missing comparison with PBFM (Baldan et al. 2025) which appears directly comparable in motivation and methodology; insufficient contrasts with other recent physics-constrained generative approaches
Inverse problem component underdeveloped: no rigorous metrics for parameter recovery quality, relies on visual inspection, lacks comparison with Bayesian inverse methods, no identifiability analysis

Inverse predictor φ is critical bottleneck yet lacks sensitivity analysis; no ablation on φ training data/architecture; paper acknowledges degraded performance (acoustic blurring) but doesn't analyze error propagation

Substantial hyperparameter complexity (λx, λf, λα, σ_min, σ_max, N_test, K_sub, K_last, clipping) with insufficient guidance for new problems; hyperparameters vary significantly across tasks; λf requires careful tuning to avoid mode collapse

Gap between theory (f=0) and practice (f≠0); heuristic modifications (memoryless noise with offset, geometric subdivision, loss clipping) lack rigorous justification; no convergence analysis of full algorithm
Computational cost not analyzed; no comparison with alternatives (PBFM, end-to-end training); scalability to high-dimensional parameters or larger grids unclear

Generalization concerns: only synthetic low-fidelity training data; misspecification experiment limited to single boundary condition type; no out-of-distribution testing; unclear if approach scales to real-world systems

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing parameter-dependent PDE constraints without paired training data, highly relevant for scientific discovery
Comprehensive experimental validation across four PDE systems with careful ablation studies isolating joint evolution contribution
Exceptional reproducibility: detailed appendices with hyperparameters, architectures, training procedures, and implementation heuristics
Principled technical approach using weak-form residuals with proper test function design and theoretical justification for scaled noise schedule (Lemma 1)
Practical efficiency with lightweight fine-tuning (15 min to 2 hours) and no inference-time overhead
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and extensive non-curated sample galleries demonstrating robustness to misspecification
weaknesses: Limited core technical novelty: primarily combines existing components (Adjoint Matching + weak residuals + inverse predictor); joint evolution of parameters is incremental
Inconsistent parameter recovery quality (MMDα ≈0.008 in Darcy but 0.06-0.35 in elasticity/Stokes) with insufficient analysis of when/why recovery succeeds or fails
Narrow experimental scope: all 2D 64×64 problems; scalability to 3D, realistic resolutions, and complex PDEs completely unexplored
Significant discrepancy between weak and strong residuals (10-100× gap) not adequately analyzed; unclear if weak-residual minimization guarantees true solution quality
High hyperparameter complexity (λx, λα, λf, κ, q, K, etc.) with incomplete sensitivity analysis; design choices appear ad-hoc (modified ηt, grid-based test centers)
Incomplete baseline comparisons: PBFM acknowledged as unfair, ECI only shown for elasticity, guidance quality only qualitative, no modern data-assimilation comparisons
No theoretical analysis of convergence, failure modes, or when method will struggle (nonlinearity, bifurcations, chaotic dynamics)
Natural image recoloring experiment feels disconnected from PDE-focused narrative with ad-hoc parametrization
